name: Bathyal-Sanctum
description: Glacier upon glacier, blue-white and creaking, buried in places by nitrogen snow. The shell is broken in places by a binary sunset, and through those breaches the deep ocean breathes plumes of frost into the dark.
The air carries burnt sugar and sulfur, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts.
Core samples from the deep crust contain isotopes with no known decay chain. The samples are stored off-world now, and studied reluctantly.
Opportunity here wears armor. Claims on nitrogen are staked, defended, and occasionally avenged, and the nearest law is a week's burn away.
